top_temples.name: Bhadrakali Temple
top_temples.location_note: Within Bhadra Fort (built 1411), Ahmedabad; the oldest temple in the city, dating to when Ahmedabad was known as Karnavati, considered one of the Shakti Peethas.

top_temples.name: Hutheesing Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ahmedabad; built 1850 AD by Seth Hutheesing, a double-storied white marble monument.

top_temples.name: Shri Hanuman Ji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Cantonment area, Ahmedabad; believed constructed about a century ago by Pandit Gajanan Prasad.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple, Jamalpur
top_temples.location_note: Jamalpur, Ahmedabad, on the eastern bank of the Sabarmati river; built over 460 years ago, centre of Ahmedabad's annual Rath Yatra.

top_temples.name: Vaishno Devi Temple, Ahmedabad
top_temples.location_note: On the Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar road; a replica of the Himalayan Vaishno Devi shrine in Jammu and Kashmir.

top_temples.name: Swaminarayan Temple, Anand
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Anand city; a six-storied temple known for its architecture.

top_temples.name: Jalaram Temple, Anand
top_temples.location_note: Anand city.

top_temples.name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Anand
top_temples.location_note: Anand; built by the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in traditional Indian architectural style, distinct from the older Swaminarayan Temple in the city.

top_temples.name: Lambhvel Hanumanji Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near Anand; a peaceful shrine surrounded by nature.

top_temples.name: Manilakshmi Jain Tirtha
top_temples.location_note: Manej village near Anand; a major Jain pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Nishkalank Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Koliyak Beach, Bhavnagar; a rare sea temple submerged at high tide and revealed at low tide.

top_temples.name: Shree Takhteshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: On a small hill in the middle of Bhavnagar city; built in 1893, named for Maharaja Takhtsinhji.

top_temples.name: Shree Khodiyar Mata Mandir, Bhavnagar
top_temples.location_note: Bhavnagar; constructed in 1911 by the then Maharaja of Bhavnagar.

top_temples.name: Aksharwadi Swaminarayan Temple (BAPS)
top_temples.location_note: Bhavnagar; a centre for worship and learning.

top_temples.name: Shri Adishwar Temple, Bhavnagar
top_temples.location_note: Bhavnagar city; a notable Jain shrine.

top_temples.name: BAPS Akshardham Temple, Gandhinagar
top_temples.location_note: Sector 20, Gandhinagar; built in 1992 by BAPS, a modern architectural masterpiece with the Yagnapurush Kund and light-and-sound shows. (Note: sometimes loosely described as an 'Ahmedabad' attraction due to the cities' proximity, but it is located in Gandhinagar.)

top_temples.name: Shree Dholeshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Gandhinagar; an ancient temple believed to predate the Mahabharata era.

top_temples.name: Mahudi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Mahudi town, Gandhinagar district; a highly revered Jain pilgrimage site established by a Jain monk in 1917.

top_temples.name: Omkareshwar Mahadev Temple, Gandhinagar
top_temples.location_note: Gandhinagar.

top_temples.name: Shree Hanuman Temple, Gandhinagar
top_temples.location_note: Gandhinagar.

top_temples.name: Zand Hanuman Temple
top_temples.location_note: Godhra, Panchmahal district.

top_temples.name: Trimurti Temple, Bhamaiya
top_temples.location_note: Bhamaiya area, Ahmedabad Road, Godhra; a large Panchmahal-district landmark.

top_temples.name: Shri Vasupujya Swami Jain Derasar
top_temples.location_note: Bamroli Road area, Godhra; a Shwetamber Jain temple.

top_temples.name: Ramji Mandir, Godhra
top_temples.location_note: Godhra city.

top_temples.name: Godhra Trimandir
top_temples.deity: Jain, Shaivite, and Vaishnavite deities together
top_temples.location_note: Near Bhamaiya village, 4.5 km from Godhra on NH 59; a non-sectarian temple housing deities from multiple traditions.

top_temples.name: Bala Hanuman Temple
top_temples.location_note: South-eastern side of Ranmal Lake, Jamnagar; holds a Guinness World Record for continuous chanting of the Ram-dhun since August 1964.

top_temples.name: Khijada Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jamnagar; established in 1630 by Nijand Acharya Shri Devchandrajia, the most-visited temple in the city.

top_temples.name: Dwarkadhish Temple, Jamnagar
top_temples.location_note: Jamnagar; a locally built temple believed founded by Vajranabh, Krishna's great-grandson, distinct from the larger Dwarkadhish Temple in Dwarka town itself.

top_temples.name: Jain Temple Triad, Jamnagar
top_temples.location_note: Jamnagar; built between 1574 and 1622.

top_temples.name: Bhidbhanjan Temple, Jamnagar
top_temples.location_note: Jamnagar; built in the 17th century, a lesser-known but historic shrine.

top_temples.name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir (Radha Ramana Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Jawahar Road, Junagadh town; ordered built by Swaminarayan himself.

top_temples.name: Shri Radha Damodarji Temple (Damodar Kund)
top_temples.location_note: On the road to Girnar within Junagadh town; adjacent to the sacred Damodar Kund, closely tied to the 15th-century poet-saint Narsinh Mehta.

top_temples.name: Bhavnath Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bhavnath Taleti, at the foot of Girnar within Junagadh town limits; site of the major annual Bhavnath Mela during Shivratri, distinct from the temples higher up on Girnar hill itself.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Junagadh
top_temples.location_note: Junagadh town.

top_temples.name: Jhulelal Mandir, Junagadh
top_temples.location_note: Junagadh town.

top_temples.name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Rajkot
top_temples.location_note: Kalawad Road, Rajkot; built in 1998 by the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

top_temples.name: Shree Panchnath Mahadev Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Panchnath main road, centre of Rajkot city.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple (Sri Radha Neelmadhav Dham)
top_temples.location_note: Kalwad Main Road, Rajkot.

top_temples.name: Shree Balaji Hanumanji Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Near the bus stand, central Rajkot; one of the city's oldest heritage temples.

top_temples.name: Parshuram Temple, Rajkot
top_temples.location_note: Rajkot city; a well-known local pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Ambika Niketan Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Tapi River, Surat; built in 1969.

top_temples.name: Shri Swaminarayan Temple, Surat
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Surat city; managed by the Shree Swaminarayan Mandir Vadtal Sansthan.

top_temples.name: Sri Sri Radha Damodar Temple (ISKCON Surat)
top_temples.location_note: Surat.

top_temples.name: Kanteshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Surat; one of the city's oldest temples, according to local tradition established by Kunti and the Pandavas.

top_temples.name: Bada Ganesh Temple, Surat
top_temples.location_note: Surat; known for its grand Ganesh idol.

top_temples.name: EME Temple (Dakshinamurthy Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Built by the Mechanical and Electrical Engineering Corps, Vadodara; architecturally represents five major world religions.

top_temples.name: Tapovan Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 7 km from Vadodara Railway Station, inside the Petrochemical Township; blends Gujarat Sompura and Rajasthani Khamira architectural styles across 4 acres.

top_temples.name: Shri Surya Narayan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atladara, about 4 km from central Vadodara; chariot-shaped architecture with seven horses symbolizing the week's days.

top_temples.name: Kayavarohan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kayavarohan town, about 30 km from Vadodara within Vadodara district; one of the 68 traditional Shiva tirthas, significant to the Pashupata sect.

top_temples.name: Kirti Mandir, Vadodara
top_temples.deity: Family temple of the Gaekwad dynasty
top_temples.location_note: Vadodara city; a historic temple associated with the former royal family.

top_temples.name: Ambaji Temple (Arasuri Ambaji Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Ambaji town, Banaskantha district, in the Aravalli Hills; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, unique for having no idol, only the sacred Shri Visa Yantra.

top_temples.name: Gabbar Hill Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Gabbar Hill near Ambaji town; considered the original abode of the goddess, distinct from the main Ambaji temple below.

top_temples.name: Ranchhodrai Temple
top_temples.location_note: Dakor's central shrine; a major Vaishnavite pilgrimage site, especially during Sharad Purnima.

top_temples.name: Danknath Temple
top_temples.location_note: By Gomti Lake next to the Ranchhodrai Temple in Dakor; historically the town's original pilgrimage shrine before Dakor became a Vaishnavite centre in 1772.

top_temples.name: Dwarkadhish Temple (Jagat Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Dwarka's central shrine; built over 2,200 years ago, part of the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit.

top_temples.name: Rukmini Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 2 km from the Dwarkadhish Temple in Dwarka; one of the few temples dedicated solely to Rukmini.

top_temples.name: Neminath Jain Temple, Girnar
top_temples.location_note: Girnar Hill; the largest and oldest of the Girnar Jain temples, dating to the 12th century, reflecting the hill's status as a major Jain pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Amba Mata Temple, Girnar
top_temples.location_note: Atop the first peak of Girnar Hill; visited by newly-weds seeking a happy marriage, representing the hill's Hindu pilgrimage tradition alongside its Jain temples.

top_temples.name: Modhera Sun Temple
top_temples.location_note: Modhera's defining monument; built in the 11th century by the Solanki dynasty, a masterpiece of Indian temple architecture.

top_temples.name: Panchlinga Shiva Temple
top_temples.location_note: Within the same Modhera Sun Temple complex, opposite the Sabha Mandapa; the only temple in the complex still actively worshipped, having survived Alauddin Khilji's destruction of the main Sun idol.

top_temples.name: Adishwar Temple (Rishabhdev Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Atop Shatrunjaya Hill, Palitana; the holiest shrine of the Svetambara Murtipujaka Jain sect, centre of the largest temple complex in the world with nearly 900 temples.

top_temples.name: Motishah Tuk
top_temples.location_note: Within the same Shatrunjaya Hill complex in Palitana; built 1829-1836 by Seth Motishah, itself a cluster of large and small temples with about 5,000 carved images.

top_temples.name: Kalika Mata Temple, Pavagadh
top_temples.location_note: At the summit of Pavagadh Hill; a 10th-11th century Shakti Peetha, part of the UNESCO Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park.

top_temples.name: Lakulisha Temple, Pavagadh
top_temples.location_note: Midway up Pavagadh Hill beside a pond, within the same archaeological park; a 10th-11th century shrine, now in ruins, dedicated to the founder of the Pashupata Shaivite sect.

top_temples.name: Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple
top_temples.location_note: Somnath's central shrine on Gujarat's western coast; the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, of Char Dham-tier significance.

top_temples.name: Somnath Mahadev Temple (Ahilyabai Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Adjacent to the main Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple; rebuilt in 1782 by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar, a distinct historic shrine at the same site.
